name: Quick Aid HELD-OUT set 4 (fresh, grounded in external clinical sources where noted)
labelling_policy: Same policy as symptom_cases.json. Cases marked with a "source" field take their ground truth from an independently published clinical reference (WHO IMCI, WHO/Govt-of-India obstetric danger signs, NHS falls/sepsis guidance), not from the developer's own judgement alone - see each case's "source" field and HOLDOUT4_RESULT.md for the search queries used. Written to specifically cover children, pregnancy, older adults (including atypical presentation - confusion/falls WITHOUT fever, a known difficult pattern), contradictory/hedging descriptions, and realistic misspellings/Indian-English colloquialisms. Run ONCE. Per explicit instruction this round, rule changes are NOT made in response to this specific run's failures - see HOLDOUT4_RESULT.md for what was found and the decision to leave it unfixed pending a dedicated, separately-reviewed round.
limitations: Written by the project developers (with external clinical sources for the three named categories), not clinician-validated as a whole, small. Several cases are deliberately hedging/contradictory, which has no single obviously "correct" machine answer - the labels reflect the safety-first reading (treat ambiguity suggestive of an emergency as an emergency), not a clinical certainty.
